description: Write the first 30 documentation articles as MDX files covering the most critical user-facing topics: Getting Started (8), Contacts & Companies (8), Deals & Pipeline (7), and Communication basics (7). All content must be written from the end-user perspective describing UI workflows and capabilities. NEVER reference internal tech stack (Next.js, React, PostgreSQL, Drizzle, Tailwind, Vercel, Redis, TypeScript).
steps: Create app/(marketing)/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx - the catch-all route that dynamically imports and renders MDX content. It should: (a) receive the slug segments, (b) look up metadata from the docs tree, (c) dynamically import the MDX file, (d) render it wrapped in the mdx-components providers, (e) generate metadata (title, description) for SEO, (f) render DocsTableOfContents, DocsBreadcrumb, DocsPrevNext around the content.
Create content/docs/ directory at project root for all MDX article files organized by section folder.

Write Getting Started section (8 articles) in content/docs/getting-started/: (1) introduction.mdx - what NuCRM is, who it's for, key capabilities overview. (2) creating-account.mdx - signup flow, workspace creation, first login. (3) workspace-setup.mdx - branding, timezone, currency, team invite. (4) importing-data.mdx - CSV import, field mapping, handling duplicates. (5) navigation-overview.mdx - sidebar, command palette (Cmd+K), keyboard shortcuts, dark mode. (6) first-contact.mdx - creating a contact, adding notes, timeline. (7) first-deal.mdx - creating a deal, moving through pipeline stages. (8) invite-team.mdx - inviting users, assigning roles, understanding permissions.

Write Contacts & Companies section (8 articles) in content/docs/contacts/: (1) managing-contacts.mdx - list view, filters, saved views, bulk ops. (2) contact-details.mdx - profile, timeline, linked entities, custom fields. (3) companies.mdx - creating companies, linking contacts, hierarchy. (4) segments.mdx - dynamic segments, filter rules, segment-based actions. (5) lifecycle-stages.mdx - lead/contact/customer stages, automatic transitions. (6) lead-scoring.mdx - BANT scoring, AI scoring, custom rules. (7) duplicate-detection.mdx - merge detection, manual merge, bulk dedup. (8) import-export.mdx - CSV import with mapping, export options, scheduling.

Write Deals & Pipeline section (7 articles) in content/docs/deals/: (1) pipeline-overview.mdx - kanban view, drag-drop, multiple pipelines. (2) creating-deals.mdx - deal creation, required fields, linking to contacts. (3) deal-stages.mdx - customizing stages, win probability, stage automation. (4) forecasting.mdx - revenue forecasting, weighted pipeline, reports. (5) multi-currency.mdx - currency settings, exchange rates, deal values. (6) deal-activities.mdx - logging calls, meetings, notes on deals. (7) won-lost-analysis.mdx - win/loss reasons, performance metrics.

Write Communication basics section (7 articles) in content/docs/communication/: (1) email-overview.mdx - sending email from CRM, templates, tracking. (2) email-sync.mdx - Gmail/Outlook 2-way sync setup, auto-logging. (3) email-templates.mdx - creating templates, variables, personalization. (4) email-tracking.mdx - open tracking, click tracking, analytics. (5) whatsapp.mdx - WhatsApp Business setup, templates, campaigns. (6) sms.mdx - SMS sending, templates, automation triggers. (7) notifications.mdx - in-app notifications, email digests, real-time alerts.

Each MDX article should be 400-800 words of genuine procedural content describing how the user performs actions in the UI. Use Markdown headings (## for major sections, ### for sub-sections), ordered lists for step-by-step procedures, unordered lists for feature enumerations, callout components for tips/warnings, and tables where appropriate. Include realistic examples (e.g., example contact fields, example pipeline stages).
acceptance_criteria: app/(marketing)/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx correctly resolves slugs to MDX content
30 MDX files exist in content/docs/ across 4 section folders
Each article is 400-800 words of genuine procedural end-user documentation
No article references internal tech stack (Next.js, React, PostgreSQL, etc.)
Articles use callout components, step lists, and proper heading hierarchy
Each article has frontmatter or metadata with title and description
verification: Run typecheck: export NVM_DIR='/root/.nvm' && . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" && cd /projects/sandbox/nucrm-bigplan-by-vm-enterprise-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit --pretty
Verify no tech stack leaks: grep -r 'Next.js\|PostgreSQL\|Drizzle\|Tailwind\|Vercel\|Redis\|TypeScript\|React' content/docs/ (should return nothing)
